executiveSummary: GM0743 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 28 neighbourhoods, three BAG places, 20 BRT settlements, logical transport links, null semantics, arithmetic, causal ledgers, zero-intensity behavior and recovery guards are coherent. Release is nevertheless correction-required because the named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Asten sustained direct inundation stress from a synthetic 50 km line-distance field. The definitive Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost profile states that the region is outside direct influence of the sea and major rivers, while separately documenting real local Aa/Dommel catchment, beek-valley, drainage and high-water backwater mechanisms. The model emits 0.537988 internal inundation-stress amplitude at T+12 through T+72 and 2,683 people under pressure by T+72, then allocates that unsupported municipality forcing to every neighbourhood using a deterministic hash. Asten's adopted 2026 water and sewer programme and Aa en Maas sources provide a much stronger basis for distinct local pluvial, Aa/Astense Aa and drainage cases. Groote Peel nature-fire exposure is real, but the default remote wildfire correctly has zero direct flame and therefore does not test Asten's local fire footprint. The new public water layer usefully shows 90 official-context objects, including RWZI Asten, but is intentionally partial and non-causal. All eight utility views correctly call their shared A67/N279 flows logical transfer proxies; unavailable drinking-water, telecom, supply, live asset, crew, backup and restoration data were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, definitief versie 1.0
supports: Asten is one of the 21 municipalities in the regional profile, and the region is stated to be outside direct influence of the sea and major rivers.
High major-river levels may still impede regional drainage, while smaller Aa/Dommel catchments and regional barriers create a different local flood mechanism.
Groote Peel and the major 2020 nature fire establish local nature-fire relevance.

RWZI Asten and wastewater pumps are explicitly electricity-dependent; many do not have structural emergency power, and the profile documents cascades across electricity, telecom, water/drainage, traffic and facilities.

This strategic PDF is current primary risk evidence but is not a machine-readable hydraulic footprint, utility topology, live incident feed or restoration inventory; no reuse licence or fixed refresh cadence is stated on the document.

evidenceSources.title: Water- en rioleringsprogramma gemeente Asten 2026–2030
supports: Asten lies between the Aa, Astense Aa and Groote Peel and contains both higher sandy ground and lower stream valleys; water measures must therefore be location-specific.

The adopted programme inventories 112 km gravity sewer, 13 pumps, 7 km infiltration sewer, seven storage/settling basins, 453 pressure-sewer units, 11 intermediate pumps, 99 km pressure sewer, 8 km drainage and two drainage pumps.

The programme identifies extreme rain, drought, heat and watercourse flooding, known nuisance locations, water retention in the Peel and drainage/storage in valleys, and requires 60 mm rainwater storage for new development.

The policy is evaluated every four years. The official HTML is municipality-scale policy/inventory evidence, not a machine API, live pump state or licensed operational topology; the publication exposes no explicit redistribution licence.

evidenceSources.title: Project 't Aa-dal Zuid
supports: The Aa and Kleine Aa water system in Asten and Someren is being made climate-robust with water retention, storage and level-management measures.
Completed Beekerloop, Aa and Kleine Aa measures confirm a local catchment mechanism that must remain distinct from direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation.
This authoritative project page is location-specific but has no fixed update cadence, machine geometry or explicit reuse licence suitable for direct simulation ingestion.

transport.summary: Four NWB-derived cross-boundary routes and scheduled-transit context are structurally coherent as static inputs.
notes: The four routes are A67 to Someren and Deurne and N279 to Deurne and Peel en Maas; every municipality endpoint resolves.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative sources establish local stream-valley, drainage, nature-fire and electricity-cascade mechanisms that the generic first-72-hour model only partially represents.
notes: E03 explicitly separates absence of direct sea/major-river influence from real high-river backwater, Aa/Dommel catchment and regional-barrier effects.
E04/E05 document the Aa, Astense Aa, Kleine Aa, high sandy areas, low valleys, Peel retention, local storage/level management, known nuisance points and a substantial sewer/drainage inventory.
E03 identifies Groote Peel nature-fire risk and an electricity dependency for RWZI Asten and many wastewater pumps, but does not provide operational controls, backup or response resources.
The public context layer exposes 90 intersecting water objects—84 weirs, two surface-water pumps, three sewer pumps and RWZI Asten—without allowing them to affect simulation.
No sensitive utility topology, live incident/asset state, crew, fuel, priority-customer list, facility capacity, stock or operator restoration promise was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.506719, pluvial 0.296049, river 0.168631, coastal 0, heat 0.485599, winter 0.788038, cyber 0.578289, earthquake 0.006293, wildfire 0.122797 and compound 0.832944.

At T+24 the compound frame had rain 41.543536 mm/h, inundation-stress amplitude 0.216151, wind 25.239709 m/s, cyber disruption 0.507332, system pressure 0.586715 and 10,941 modeled residents under pressure.

At T+72 compound retained inundation-stress amplitude 0.216151 and cyber disruption 0.065984, with pressure 0.612051, 11,562 modeled residents under pressure and 543,160 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.
apps/web/src/scenarios.ts clones the canonical sim-core presets, so the audited configurations equal the user-selectable scenarios.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden and municipality/local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0743 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 27.40 seconds.
Every canonical preset with intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated T+24 frames were byte-deterministic; state remained finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours were monotonic; route flow never exceeded effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciled municipality population 17,385, affected population 10,941, demand and delivery exactly across all eight services.
Changing among all 11 map layers left physical hazard, municipality pressure and affected population invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The named direct major-river forcing contradicts the regional profile, and neighbourhood hazard placement is not based on Asten's terrain or water system.
notes: Canonical river-flood reports internal inundation stress 0 at T+0, 0.189372 at T+6 and 0.537988 at T+12/24/48/72; E03 says the region is outside direct sea and major-river influence.
That frame grows from 49 modeled people under pressure at T+12 to 1,943 at T+24 and 2,683 at T+48/T+72, with cumulative proxy person-hours 15,380, 50,708, 128,374 and 206,237 respectively.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts riverExposure() uses distance from the municipality centre to three coarse diagonal segments and returns exp(-distance/24) within 50 km; it has no Aa/Astense Aa catchment, barrier, water level, discharge constraint, breach, arrival or LIWO mask.

Every neighbourhood then receives municipality hazard severity multiplied by 0.82–1.18 using hazardSeed. At river T+24 Voordeldonk ranks 0.198756, Ommel centrum 0.198737 and Ostade 0.197113, while De Groote Peel is 0.145820; this ordering is deterministic but not hydraulic evidence.

Pluvial risk is locally plausible, but its 0.208617 T+24 internal stress and 4,240 modeled people under pressure still derive from density, preset forcing and seeds rather than the documented high/low terrain, sewers, pumps, basins, Aa system or nuisance locations.
The default remote wildfire yields zero direct flame, smoke 0.257414 and drought 0.594288 at T+24; this is coherent for that named remote event but does not test a local Groote Peel ignition.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances are inspectable, but the first-72-hour magnitudes are not calibrated to Asten's public assets or physical networks.
notes: River T+24 availability was power 0.903540, water 0.720792, drainage 0.653271, gas 0.866076, telecom 0.658128, mobility 0.862074, facilities 0.864478 and supply 0.635498.
Compound T+24 availability was power 0.162192, water 0.463652, drainage 0.358698, gas 0.625484, telecom 0.358976, mobility 0.340969, facilities 0.656410 and supply 0.447189.
E03 supports directional dependencies—particularly electricity into telecom, water/wastewater, mobility and facilities—but it does not calibrate these exact availability values.

The simulation has no explicit RWZI Asten, municipal sewer/drainage pump, basin, pressure-sewer, Brabant Water pressure zone, Enexis asset, telecom site, facility role or supply-stock node in its causal graph.
All eight service views reuse the same four A67/N279 corridors and nominal capacity 820; every route correctly declares transferSemantics logical-proxy.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus contribution deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure terms sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, driver metadata, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness affects modeled population/supply burden after physical pressure and does not alter hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated intervention effects are labeled scenario assumptions, while the common road-derived utility corridors remain logical proxies.
Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure as a planning approximation, not observed outage-customer-hours, casualties or displacement.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and intervention-delay guards behave consistently, but invalid river forcing and absent local resources prevent operational interpretation.
notes: River forcing remains active at T+72, every service recovery-progress value remains exactly zero, and the model avoids a generic all-clear while water persists; the premise is nevertheless unsupported for direct major-river flooding in Asten.
River T+72 leaves seven service availabilities at T+24 values while facilities declines from 0.864478 to 0.648721 through modeled dependencies; this is not an Asten operator or care forecast.
Compound residual water blocks generic restoration at T+72; power remains limiting at 0.157553 and telecom/mobility/facilities/supply are 0.348109/0.330700/0.508018/0.442133.
Ended storm, pluvial, winter, wildfire and earthquake forcing recovers monotonically; heat/drought and cyber retain bounded forcing under their scenario schedules.
Actual water-control state, utility switching, wastewater backup, roads, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staffing, stock and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A synthetic proximity corridor creates unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation in Asten.
findings.evidence: E03 states that Zuidoost-Brabant is outside direct influence of the sea and major rivers, while carefully preserving an indirect high-water/backwater mechanism and local Aa/Dommel catchment flooding. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-455 instead measures Asten's centre to three coarse diagonal segments and returns positive riverExposure inside 50 km; lines 584-589 turn it into municipality-wide forcing for the canonical preset explicitly titled ‘Rhine, Meuse & IJssel high water’. The exact frame emits internal inundation stress 0.537988 from T+12 through T+72, pressure 0.219325 and 1,943 people under pressure at T+24, and pressure 0.249531, 2,683 people and 206,237 cumulative event-attributable service person-hours at T+72. All eight recovery-progress values remain zero because the fabricated direct water persists. This is municipality-specific evidence of the shared national line-distance defect, not a claim that Asten lacks local or indirect water risk.
findings.action: Add GM0743 to the audited interim direct-major-river exclusion, with an evidence note saying local Aa/Astense Aa and major-river backwater effects remain unresolved rather than safe. The durable fix must replace code lists and diagonal corridors with a selected LIWO/source-specific connected footprint, and model local Aa/stream-valley/backwater scenarios separately. Direct water must be zero unless the selected authoritative scenario intersects GM0743; indirect service/supply consequences may remain only through an explicit, named mechanism.

findings.summary: Neighbourhood water allocation is seeded rather than tied to Asten's documented high ground, stream valleys, assets or nuisance locations.
findings.evidence: E04 distinguishes higher sandy ground, lower beekdalen, Peel retention and valley storage/drainage, and inventories sewers, pumps and basins; E05 supplies the Aa/Kleine Aa catchment context. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3319-3333 instead sets local hazard severity to municipality severity × (0.82 + hazardSeed × 0.36). For river T+24 all 28 neighbourhoods receive the unsupported scalar, with Voordeldonk 0.198756, Ommel centrum 0.198737 and Ostade 0.197113 highest and De Groote Peel 0.145820. For pluvial T+24 the model emits 0.208617 internal stress, pressure 0.313097 and 4,240 people under pressure without intersecting a terrain, catchment, sewer or measured nuisance layer. The values are deterministic but not a local footprint.
findings.action: Replace seeded direct-water rank with intersected, versioned source layers: approved hydraulic scenario geometry where available, AHN terrain, IMWA surface-water/barrier objects and vetted local stress-test data. Preserve no-data, keep pluvial, local stream, regional barrier, groundwater and direct major-river mechanisms separate, and do not display metre depth unless the selected product is calibrated depth.

findings.summary: Asten's documented drainage system and power-dependent wastewater assets are absent from pluvial service causality.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 identify RWZI Asten, pump dependence on electricity, 112 km gravity sewer, 13 pumps, seven basins, 453 pressure-sewer units, 11 intermediate pumps and two drainage pumps. E07/E08 provide some safe public point objects. Yet pluvial T+24 drainage availability 0.407370 is derived from generic hazard, dependency and network terms; no named pump, basin, catchment or wastewater-treatment node can fail, receive backup or explain recovery. The public layer's 90 local objects explicitly do not affect simulation.
findings.action: Add a non-sensitive public water-asset/catchment adapter with provenance and explicit completeness. Use public objects as context first; connect only operator-approved dependencies and capacities. Where controls, topology, backup and live state are unavailable or security-sensitive, retain a bounded service-specific synthetic fallback labeled scenario rather than inferring them.

findings.summary: The default remote wildfire does not test Asten's locally important Groote Peel flame footprint.
findings.evidence: E03 records Groote Peel nature-fire relevance and the consequential 2020 fire. The canonical remote wildfire produces direct flame exactly zero at T+12/T+24, with smoke 0.257414, drought 0.594288, peak severity 0.122797 and only four modeled people under pressure at T+24. This is coherent for the preset's remote epicentre, but it is not evidence that a local Peel incident is harmless and it contains no local fuels, peat/vegetation condition, moisture, wind-aware spread, water points, access or suppression state.
findings.action: Keep direct flame and smoke separate and require an explicit local incident/epicentre for a Groote Peel exercise. Intersect fire spread with authoritative combustible land cover and municipality/neighbourhood polygons; preserve the current growing circle only as a clearly synthetic fallback and do not infer suppression resources.

findings.summary: The public water overlay is useful and honestly non-causal, but it is not a complete Asten sewer or water-system inventory.
findings.evidence: The 2026-09-02 snapshot intersects GM0743 with 84 weirs, surface-water pumps 287PWG and 323KNL, sewer pumps Rioolgemaal Ommel (published capacity 80), De Hutten (350) and Heusden (100), and RWZI Asten. Its collection declares evidenceClass official-context, affectsSimulation false and partial national contributor coverage. E04 independently documents materially more municipal sewer/drainage infrastructure—13 gravity-system pumps, 453 pressure units, 11 intermediate pumps and two drainage pumps—so the six pump objects are not a completeness claim. The UI labels the overlay ‘Official water assets’ and did not turn presence into operational availability.
findings.action: Retain the official-context/non-causal semantics, publisher object ids, retrievedAt, licence and partial-coverage warning. Add municipal/GWSW coverage only when reuse and freshness are verified; distinguish municipal sewer, water-board surface-water, wastewater-treatment and drinking-water classes, and never infer connectivity, capacity or live state from a point.

findings.summary: Every essential service reuses four road corridors rather than Asten-specific utility or care/supply topology.
findings.evidence: Power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply all expose exactly the same A67-to-Someren, A67-to-Deurne and two N279 edges with generalized nominal capacity sum 820. E06 supports road geometry only, while E03 supports dependency direction but not topology/capacity. The implementation and UI correctly label every transfer logical-proxy and the map fidelity line says ‘Official geography & transport · logical service transfers · scenario impacts’, preventing an explicit physical-network misstatement.
findings.action: Keep the fidelity disclosure. Add independently licensed public asset context per service, but promote a flow to physical only with operator-approved topology, capacity, direction, backup and current state. Otherwise retain distinct, inspectable service-specific synthetic/logical graphs rather than cloning road capacity into cable, pipe, telecom, care or food claims.

findings.summary: First-72-hour service levels lack local operator, facility, stock, backup and restoration calibration.
findings.evidence: The eight balances and dependencies close, but river T+24 availability ranges from supply 0.635498 to power 0.903540 and compound T+24 from power 0.162192 to facilities 0.656410 without a named Enexis asset, Brabant Water pressure zone, telecom site, facility role, supermarket/depot, vehicle, crew or restoration estimate. E03 validates cascades and flags wastewater power dependence, not these exact magnitudes. Three coarse public governmental-service points and 90 partial water objects remain contextual and do not supply roles, capacity, staffing, backup, inventory or state.
findings.action: Ingest safe public static asset/role data with source date and coverage, then keep operational topology, availability, backup, stock, crews and repair time unknown unless an operator or authorized exercise dataset supplies them. Any synthetic fallback must be service-specific, bounded, editable and visibly scenario-class evidence.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter and cyber outputs are scenario stressors rather than dated Asten observations, warnings or incidents.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 support regional relevance of extreme rain/wind, heat, drought, winter disruption, cyber and utility cascades. The model peaks—storm 0.506719, heat 0.485599, winter 0.788038 and cyber 0.578289—derive from canonical schedules and deterministic seeds. At T+72 heat retains drought/current severity 0.438363/0.078905 and cyber disruption 0.057829; these are preset continuations, not a KNMI warning, measured local heat exposure, named cyber target or operator incident.
findings.action: Keep scenario/evidence confidence prominent. Optionally accept timestamped KNMI observations/warnings and an authorized incident target as separate inputs with collection-specific provenance and expiry; never describe a canonical preset as forecast, probability or live outage.

findings.summary: Coastal and Groningen-earthquake direct effects are bounded and small/zero, but remain named screening cases rather than local risk assessments.
findings.evidence: Coastal produces exactly zero direct inundation and affected population at all checkpoints while wind causes T+24 pressure 0.094756 and 9,282 cumulative proxy person-hours, keeping direct and indirect mechanisms separable. The remote Groningen earthquake peaks at severity 0.006293, has zero current shaking/affected population at T+24 and 1,821 cumulative proxy person-hours at T+72. Neither preset supplies event probability, event-specific ground motion, site response or asset fragility.
findings.action: Retain explicit remote-event naming and direct/indirect disclosure. Use event-specific KNMI ground motion and validated local vulnerability for a real earthquake, and connected source-specific hydraulic geometry for any coastal/indirect water case; do not turn zero direct forcing into a universal all-clear.

findings.summary: Official identity, rounded demography, null handling, settlements and service-specific local allocation are inspectably coherent.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 agree with GM0743 identity and headline totals. All 28 neighbourhoods retain unavailable values as null; their rounded population is only 20 above the municipality row; all three BAG place centres are inside; BRT/CBS/BAG semantics remain separate; and compound T+24 local population, affected people, demand and delivery reconcile municipality values for all services. Non-residential context influences demand without inventing residents or measured critical load.
findings.action: Retain source editions, null semantics, distinct geography products, aggregate-context disclosures and exact reconciliation tests.

findings.summary: The deterministic, causal, zero-intensity, sustained-water and UI semantic contracts pass for GM0743.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passed ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services; zero intensity exactly clears event severity/peak/affected/person-hours; T+24 repeats exactly; numerical and route bounds hold; all ledgers and counterfactuals close; map-layer selection cannot alter physics; and sustained water blocks elapsed-time restoration. A headless Chromium check selected Asten, the named river case and T+72, exercised all 11 layer buttons, displayed 36% normalized ‘inundation stress’, 2.7K people under pressure and the logical-service-transfer fidelity text, exposed official water assets, and produced no page, console or failed-local-response errors.
findings.action: Preserve these national invariants while correcting GM0743-RIVER-001; add exact Asten zero-direct-water and unsupported-evidence fixtures without weakening local/indirect water scenarios.

corrections.summary: Conservatively remove unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing from GM0743 and replace it with selected hydraulic mechanisms.
corrections.validation: Interim: add GM0743 to riverExposure()'s audited direct-major-river exclusion, attach an evidence note, and assert flood stress exactly zero at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset while separately permitted indirect network effects remain possible. Re-run pnpm test, MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0743 pnpm audit:model and MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=ALL pnpm audit:model. Durable machine source: LIWO GeoServer OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows plus catalogue API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 for source-specific national breach/depth/arrival products. LIWO is layer/release-versioned rather than fixed-cadence and its public portal did not expose a general redistribution licence during audit, so record scenario/layer/version/retrieval, review each layer's terms and do not ship cached rasters until cleared. Use Waterschapshuis surface-water IMWA OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-oppervlaktewateren-imwa/ogc/v1 (hydro-object vector, weekly, CC0) and keringen IMWA OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-keringen-imwa/ogc/v1 (barrier vector, weekly, CC0) to distinguish Aa/Astense Aa/regional barriers from major rivers, but never infer a flood extent from line presence alone. The successor fixture must apply direct water only to an approved connected scenario footprint and preserve explicit unknown/no-data.

corrections.summary: Replace seeded Asten flood/fire allocation with versioned terrain, catchment and combustible-land-cover intersections.
corrections.validation: Define source-specific local footprints carrying mechanism, source id, edition, resolution, temporal validity, units, no-data, uncertainty and licence. Preferred public machine inputs are AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities (Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK 0.5 m DTM/DSM tiles, cyclic national acquisition by AHN edition, CC0) for high/low terrain; BRT TOP10NL OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 (Kadaster native 1:10,000 vector terrain/land-cover objects, annual, CC BY 4.0) for combustible/open-water context; and the weekly CC0 IMWA surface-water API from correction 1 for Aa/Astense Aa geometry. E04 is current four-year-review municipal policy evidence but not a reusable GIS stress layer; request the underlying local stress-test/nuisance geometry and terms rather than digitizing prose. Tests must show only intersected areas receive direct water/flame, keep smoke wider than flame, never treat terrain/land cover as fuel moisture or hydraulics, and fall back to an explicitly synthetic selectable epicentre/footprint when operational incident geometry is unavailable.

corrections.summary: Use safe public Asten service assets where available and keep unavailable/security-sensitive topology and live state explicitly unknown or synthetic.
corrections.validation: Retain the existing Waterschapshuis Kunstwerken IMWA object feed https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 (object points/vectors, weekly, CC BY-SA 4.0, contributor completeness varies) and Waterketen DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 (object-level wastewater assets, cadence unknown, CC BY-SA 4.0, contributor completeness varies), with affectsSimulation false until dependencies are approved. For electricity/gas, evaluate Enexis Asset Data https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/enexis-assetdata (public line/station asset downloads, annual according to its data passport, CC0); it is static insight, not KLIC replacement, operational state, capacity or switching. For mobility retain NWB road sections (monthly, CC0) and add dated NDW operational data only with validity timestamps; NWB remains geometry, not live capacity. For public facility locations retain KVK/PDOK Overheidsdiensten https://api.pdok.nl/kvk/overheidsdiensten-geharmoniseerd/ogc/v1 (point registry, Public Domain Mark 1.0, cadence not stated, coarse/partial roles). CBS 2025 annual CC BY 4.0 businesses may inform transparent supply demand but not warehouse/supermarket stock. No adequate public operational Brabant Water pressure-zone/feed, telecom topology/current state or first-72-hour food/fuel inventory was identified; use the smallest service-specific synthetic fallback with visible scenario confidence, and never infer topology, backup, staffing, stock, crews or restoration from public asset presence.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Asten LIWO/Waterschap breach, water-level, flow, depth, arrival, catchment or defence-state layer is ingested; normalized inundation stress is not measured metres.
Removing unsupported direct major-river inundation must not erase documented Aa/Astense Aa, local stream, regional-barrier, groundwater, pluvial or high-river backwater mechanisms.
The current local water/sewer programme is authoritative policy and inventory context but is not a live machine topology, asset-state or capacity feed and publishes no explicit reuse licence.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic hashes do not resolve parcels, buildings, elevation, cellars, ditches, barriers, sewers, pumps, households, workers, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; its 90 intersecting objects cannot be reconciled as a complete inventory against differently scoped municipal sewer assets.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, combustible-fuel condition, peat/soil moisture, wind-aware spread, smoke dispersion, access, evacuation, suppression and fire-water state.

The remote Groningen-earthquake preset lacks occurrence probability, local site amplification, event ground motion and building/asset fragility; coastal direct zero is scenario-specific, not a universal all-clear.
No physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live closures, timetables, vehicles, bridge state, evacuation throughput or repair access.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Asten resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, dispatch, traffic restrictions and schedule transitions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
Rounded CBS values, partial suppression and distinct CBS/BAG/BRT editions prevent false exact reconciliation across geographic products.
provinceReviewFlags: Review every Noord-Brabant municipality receiving direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel stress from the shared 50 km line-distance field against its safety-region profile and an approved LIWO connected footprint; keep indirect backwater/service effects separate.

Across Aa en Maas and De Dommel municipalities, distinguish Maas/Rhine direct flooding, high-river impeded discharge, regional barriers, Aa/Dommel stream flooding, groundwater and pluvial overload before allocating neighbourhood impact.
Replace deterministic neighbourhood water ranks with coordinated AHN, IMWA and approved local stress-test/hydraulic layers; preserve source resolution, no-data, licence and scenario identity.
Use Groote Peel and other Brabant nature areas to regression-test explicit local wildfire origins and polygon/land-cover intersections while keeping remote flame and smoke mechanisms separate.

Coordinate Waterschapshuis, Enexis, KVK, NWB and CBS public context at province/operator scale, but never infer live state, sensitive topology, utility capacity, backup, stock, crews or restoration from static open data.
